tally: Ten people, still bootstrapped, and the founders say 43% of new users now arrive through AI search.
supademo: Sales and onboarding teams send an interactive walkthrough instead of a static deck. Free side tools sit in front and feed the paid product.
plutio: A freelancer otherwise keeps proposals in one app, contracts in another, and invoices in a third. Plutio is that whole pile in one login, at a size a solo founder can still imagine copying.
anonymous-workforce-management-saas: The largest Stripe-verified figure in this set has no public name and no website. Employers have been paying it for scheduling and compliance since 2021, and the listing stays anonymous.
myplots: The money is a cut of the ticket, 20% plus a dollar, not a monthly plan. That is why the last 30 days show hundreds of thousands of dollars while recurring revenue reads as zero.
supliful: A creator can put their name on a product while someone else makes and ships it. The work is operations, which is why a plan that starts near $69 a month has piled up tens of millions all-time.
salesrobot: It runs LinkedIn outreach and cold email, and customers pay for credits rather than a seat. The Stripe record shows usage, not a neat subscriber count.
codedex: Beginners practice inside a game, then a club pass starts around $9.99 a month. Thousands of those small memberships are what the revenue figure is adding up.
flocksy: The price is a studio retainer, from about $1,199 a month, because what you buy is a queue of designers and editors. A founder AMA put the team past 70 people.
mycater: Office managers already order catering every week. MyCater takes a cut of that spend, which is why the last 30 days show about $76k while recurring revenue reads as zero.
stan: Creators already need somewhere to get paid. Stan is that checkout, and the last Stripe snapshot put it near $3.57M in monthly revenue. The key expired in April 2026, so the figure is a snapshot.
windmill-growth: Founders pay about $3,999 a month so someone else writes their LinkedIn posts. Seventy-nine of those retainers are what the Stripe record is adding up.
prosp: Sales teams pay for LinkedIn outreach, and the listing itself is for sale. The Stripe key expired in February 2026, so the monthly figure is the last verified snapshot.
dataexpert-techcreator: Students pay about $119 a month for data and AI courses. Hundreds of those memberships are what the revenue figure is adding up.
controlresell: Resellers pay between $30 and $120 a month so the tool posts, negotiates, and relists for them. The Stripe record shows 442 of those subscriptions.
myfrank: Each employee gets a QR code and a challenge for collecting Google reviews. The founder has put the product up for sale.
image-charts: Developers still need a chart that shows up inside an email. The monthly figure is about $6.3k, and the all-time total has been compounding since 2017.
geswork: French service companies pay for scheduling, documents, and billing in one login. The same founder also runs Valideo, a field-report product with its own Stripe record.
mon-atelier: Repair shops in France pay from €19 a month for tickets, invoices, and the compliance ledger. One person runs it, and the founder says 48 shops signed up with no marketing spend.
conductor: Developers still need a bridge into QuickBooks Desktop. Conductor charges about $49 a month per company file for that, and the founder says churn is almost none.
calendesk: Therapists, coaches, and other service pros already book clients and take deposits. Calendesk is that workflow, priced around $79 to $147 a month.
soldcomps: Resellers price from what actually sold. SoldComps sells that eBay history as an API, from $9 to $79 a month.
medpilot: Clinics pay so someone answers after-hours calls and fills empty chairs. The last 30 days show about $44.7k, well above the listed subscription figure, because the bill mixes usage and setup.
seobot: Founders pay about $49 a month for an agent that researches keywords and publishes the blog. It was only an honorable mention on 28 September; today's Stripe sync puts it near $39.1k MRR.
heron-copier: Traders pay monthly to copy positions across cTrader, MetaTrader, and the rest, without renting a VPS. TrustMRR marks the figure Creem-verified, about $8.3k MRR.
textbee: An Android phone becomes the SMS gateway, so there is no per-message fee. The pro plan is about $9.99 a month, and TrustMRR marks the revenue Polar-verified.
quotedeck: Insurance agents pay about $60 to $140 a month to present a life or health quote as a proper document. One person runs it, and the listing has been for sale.
easy-moving-permits: Movers pay per application so the permit, the city fee, and the service charge land in one checkout. Recurring revenue reads as zero because the money is the transaction.
expensent: Receipts already sit in the inbox. Expensent forwards them to the accountant or into QuickBooks, and one person in Portugal runs it at about $845 MRR.
khosmos: French construction crews already write quotes on site. Khosmos turns that quote into a signature and an invoice, at about €24 a month.
web3forms: A static site still needs a contact form. Web3Forms posts it to email with no server, and TrustMRR marks the roughly $41k in monthly revenue as Paddle-verified.
capgo: A Capacitor app can ship a JavaScript fix without waiting on App Store review. Capgo is that update pipe, and the Stripe record shows 1,130 subscriptions.
pushouse: Merchants pay for WhatsApp broadcasts and cart messages. Pushouse is that channel, founded in January 2026, with 248 subscriptions.
helios: Fitness brands already message their members. The last 30 days show about $45.3k while listed recurring revenue reads as none, so the Stripe record looks like usage billing.
coldsire: Outbound teams pay about $6 a month per mailbox. The Stripe record shows 909 of those accounts.
hirevire: Candidates record answers to the hiring questions, so nobody books a screening call. Plans run about $49 to $249 a month.
legalone: French companies have to publish legal notices. LegalOne files them for a fee, which is why recurring revenue reads as zero while the last 30 days show about $10.7k.
promatic: Plumbing and HVAC contractors pay about $99 a job so the permit and the inspection get filed. Recurring revenue reads as zero because the bill is the project.
voxnow: Belgian law firms pay about €90 a user so a missed call becomes an email summary and an SMS. Twenty-six of those seats are the monthly figure.
fast-corp-ltd: People pay to open a Bulgarian company and then keep the books there. Formation starts around €1,500, and accounting from about €229 a month is the part that stays.
liinks: Creators pay $5 or $12 a month for one page that holds every link. The Stripe record shows 5,419 of those subscriptions.
pasul-ro: Romanian speakers book a therapist through Pasul, online or in person. The last 30 days show about $30.6k because the money is the session, not a monthly seat.
uhoh-com: Startups pay a flat monthly fee for a managed IT desk, with plans from about $3,000 a month. Thirty of those subscriptions are the Stripe figure.
angel-match: Founders pay for a searchable list of angel investors and VCs. Hundreds of those subscriptions have added up to nearly $1M all-time.
v62form: People in the UK pay once, about £11.95 to print and ship or £39.95 for the full service, to replace a lost V5C logbook. Recurring revenue reads as zero because each form is a single checkout.
karma: Teams pay about $3 a user so kudos and gift cards live inside Slack or Teams. The last 30 days show about $24.5k, above the listed seat figure, which fits annual plans and reward top-ups.
enquiry-genie: Airbnb hosts pay about £29 a month so replies to guest emails go out in their own tone, with live prices attached. Listed recurring revenue reads as none, so the last 30 days, about $9.4k, is the figure to read.
guidejar: Teams record a click-through of a workflow and share it instead of walking someone through the same steps. The free side stops at five guides, and 215 subscriptions are the paid side.
aila: US loan officers pay from about $50 a month so a discovery call gets written into the loan file. Ninety-nine of those seats are the Stripe figure.
kibu: Disability-service providers pay so the care log and the compliance paperwork live in one system. The Stripe snapshot is about $234k in monthly revenue, and the key expired in April 2026, so that figure is the last verified sync.
uk-hormone-prescribing-ops-agency: A UK hormone-prescribing service and ops agency, with no public site on the listing. The Stripe record shows 2,339 subscriptions and about $165k in monthly revenue, synced 3 October.
1lookup: Teams pay in credits to check a phone number, an email, or an IP. The last 30 days show about $390k, above the listed monthly figure, because the bill is usage. The listing is for sale at $10M.
rezi: Job seekers pay about $29 a month, or $149 once, for a resume built to pass an applicant tracking system. The Stripe record shows 10,418 of those subscriptions.
cometly: B2B teams pay to see which ads actually closed revenue. 291 of those subscriptions add up to about $206k a month.
probate-leads: Real estate investors pay about $50 to $800 a month for probate leads pulled from court filings. The listing has no public site, and the Stripe record shows 627 subscriptions.
upscale-system-llc: B2B companies pay for outbound that runs email, calls, and LinkedIn from one CRM. 289 of those subscriptions add up to about $100k a month.
cartboss: Stores pay per text when someone leaves a cart, not a monthly seat. Recurring revenue reads as zero, and the all-time total is about $1.74M.
proclinica: Spanish private clinics pay about €35 a month for the agenda, the clinical history, and the invoice. 136 of those subscriptions are the Stripe figure.
white-glove-content: People pay about $54 to $284 a month for faceless social video, delivered from a dashboard. 589 of those subscriptions are the figure, and the listing is for sale at $2.5M.
comp-ai: Startups pay about $12k a month across 49 seats so SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR evidence lives in one place. The last 30 days show about $700k, which fits annual contracts and setup packs on top of those seats.
hypeproxies: Scrapers and stores pay for residential and ISP proxies, from about $65 to $300 a month, billed as usage rather than seats. Recurring revenue reads as zero, and the last 30 days show about $320k.
convertlabs: Cleaning, lawn, and carpet businesses pay about $67 to $397 a month so bookings, payments, and the marketing site live on one screen. 474 of those subscriptions add up to about $28k a month.
simple-analytics: Agencies and teams pay for cookieless analytics that can sit next to Google Analytics. 1,263 of those subscriptions add up to about $38k a month.
stoik: European brokers sell cyber insurance with the security work attached. Seat revenue reads as zero, the last 30 days show about $40k, and the all-time total is about $23.3M.
presscart: Founders buy a press placement, about $599 on promo or $999 normally, instead of an agency retainer. Two subscriptions are the seat figure, the last 30 days show about $62k, and the Stripe key expired in July 2026.
festejar: Clubs in Catalonia pay per ticket so the agenda, the store, and the brand live on one site. Seat revenue reads as zero, and about $188k has come through since the product launched in March 2026.
ndiscompliant: Australian NDIS providers pay AUD $149 to $699 a month, or $297 once, for audit-ready policies and a gap check. Seat revenue reads as zero, and the last 30 days show about $5.6k.
friendfilter-groupfilter: People pay about $29 or $49 a month for a Chrome extension that drops inactive Facebook friends and groups. 337 of those subscriptions are the figure, the Stripe key expired in September 2026, and the listing is for sale.
